state: Can C9 requires a unique runtime occurrence identity, original native cause, and source/invocation origin for standard failures. Q requires equal error kinds to retain distinct failures, and propagation must preserve an existing occurrence rather than inventing a new one. A native Error object can be thrown independently twice; thrown primitives have no object identity. Standard-failure snapshots are opaque Can data with only kind, fixed/safely described message and occurrence ID exposed. No raw cause or stack is appended to that projection. I07 already brands primitive arithmetic/bounds causes privately. There are no external users or compatibility obligations. Options are fresh opaque tokens at originating capture with WeakMap metadata and recognition of existing tokens during propagation; caching occurrences by raw cause object; or allocating a new occurrence at every boundary including propagation. The token option preserves repeated-origin distinction and stable forwarding, but requires explicit creation/forwarding tests and private-only diagnostic access to cause/origin. Cause caching merges independent throws of a reused object; always allocating splits one propagated failure. No performance data is available.

occurrence.instructions: Which occurrence model best satisfies the supplied identity and privacy contracts without adding language semantics?

criteria.tokens: Create a new opaque occurrence for each origin, preserve recognized occurrences during forwarding, and keep cause/origin in private metadata.
criteria.cause_cache: Reuse one occurrence whenever the same native cause object appears again.
criteria.every_boundary: Allocate a fresh occurrence each time a failure crosses any boundary, even if it is already recorded.
